current_worker_packet.todo_line: - [ ] 003 Introduce and focused-test an app-owned dashboard query/view-model boundary that begins from the authenticated email and fresh active-club authority; move all projection-backed dashboard data behind one coherent socket assign, subscribe before the connected initial read, preserve route/access error semantics and transient LiveView state, and retain the existing notification predicates provisionally.
current_worker_packet.outcome: The club dashboard loads and refreshes one coherent dashboard view model from the authenticated email and freshly resolved active-club authority, stores that result under one socket assign, subscribes before the connected initial read, and preserves existing route, access, rendering, command and transient-state behavior while the current notification predicates remain provisional.
scope: Add an app-owned `MembaWeb.MemberDashboardQuery` boundary, with focused tests, that accepts the routed club identity, authenticated normalized email and selected group identity; every invocation must call `Accounts.list_active_clubs_for_email/1`, construct only the identity input needed by `MemberDashboardPresentation`, and return its coherent result or the existing `:forbidden`/`:not_found` error.

Change `MemberDashboardLive.mount/3`, `handle_params/3`, explicit command refreshes and notification refreshes to use the new query. On connected mount, subscribe to `Memba.ReadModelChanges.topic/0` before invoking the query; disconnected mount must still perform the current read.

Keep the routed club ID and authenticated identity email as stable LiveView inputs. Do not derive a later query input from the previously loaded `selected_club`, and do not use mount-captured `current_identity_clubs` as authorization for a refresh.

Store the projection-backed dashboard result under one long-lived socket assign such as `:dashboard`. Adapt event handlers and helper functions to read selected club, selected group, current member, permission flags, rows and counts from that model instead of retaining mirrored top-level socket assigns.

Adapt rendering to consume the coherent model without duplicating all of its fields into socket state. A render-local map expansion for the existing template is acceptable; if Phoenix shell metadata requires a derived `:page_title`, keep the dashboard result as its sole source and do not perform an independent read.

Preserve current `:forbidden` versus `:not_found` behavior on mount, route patches and refreshes, and preserve existing command behavior for access requests, admissions, removals and welcome delivery.

Retain the current hand-written `handle_info/2` matching semantics provisionally, including their current broad and missing cases. This slice changes their refresh target to the new query but does not introduce interests, a source adapter, bind-window reconciliation or new projector coverage.

Add focused proof that repeated query calls use fresh active-club authority, that selected-club membership loss cannot be masked by a mount-time club snapshot, that route changes still re-evaluate selected-group access, and that successful refreshes do not reset picker/query, targeted-add, removal, access-request or command feedback state. Preserve existing dashboard, admission and targeted-add regression coverage.
scope_exclusions: Do not implement the provisional generic binding, opaque interest matching, notification translator, bind-time reconciliation, reconnect contract or subscriber cleanup; those belong to tasks 004 and 005.
Do not add Person, Club, Message, represented-role or scoped collection notification handling, and do not remove the current broad MemberEmailDelivery refresh in this task.
Do not change conversation detail, delivery detail, settings, message composition, group creation, invitation, staff streams or any other LiveView.
Do not create the local Mix package or edit `web/mix.exs`, `mix.lock`, Docker files, release configuration, `bin/dev` or quality-gate wiring.
Do not edit acceptance feature files or step definitions, including the still-`@todo` iteration-067 club-member scenario.
Do not change domain commands, projector behavior, projection schemas, authorization policy, ADRs, the approved plan, the migration matrix, reference documentation, todo.md or delivery artifacts.
Do not claim the package API, interest types, source adapter, module placement beyond this app query, or reconnect hook is frozen by this slice.

references.facts: The technical model requires one coherent dashboard query result, fresh authorization on every refresh, LiveView-owned subscription, subscribe-before-read ordering and preservation of transient state. The broader bind-time reconciliation, scoped invalidation and conversation proof remain later obligations.

ADR 0027 requires each view-specific query to return one coherent view model for one assign, with an authorized reread on relevant changes; club home must begin as one dashboard model rather than separately refreshed fields.

Committed projection notifications are broadcast on the shared PubSub topic as `{:read_model_changed, %{projector: ..., source_event: ..., metadata: ..., changes: ...}}`. This task retains the dashboard's current filters but moves subscription before the connected read.

The accepted matrix records that MemberDashboardLive currently spreads one composed result across ordinary assigns, reads before subscribing and refreshes with mount-captured active clubs. It identifies route IDs, picker/admission/removal/access-request state as LiveView-owned and requires fresh authority beginning from authenticated email.

`mount/3` currently calls `MemberDashboardPresentation.load/4` before subscribing and fans `dashboard_assigns` into the socket. `refresh_dashboard/3` reuses `current_identity_clubs`; handlers and command helpers read selected club, selected group, current member and permission flags from top-level assigns. Existing handle_info clauses broadly refresh for all MemberEmailDelivery changes and same-club configured projectors.

`load/4` already composes selected club/member authorization, discoverable and participating groups, permissions, members, counts, conversations, admission candidates and group email data into one result map. It accepts caller-supplied active clubs, so the new query must supply a fresh list on every invocation while preserving `:forbidden` and `:not_found` distinctions.

`Accounts.list_active_clubs_for_email/1` normalizes the email and reads the current active club projections. It is the required fresh starting point instead of `current_identity_clubs` captured during mount.

The dashboard template currently consumes flat assigns for selected club/group, groups, permissions, member rows, counts and message rows. Rendering may expand the coherent dashboard model locally, but these values must no longer be duplicated as long-lived socket assigns.

Existing coverage includes routed rendering, group discovery, access loss, route-patch authorization rechecks, current-actor role loss, conversation-access changes, member rows/counts and initial role badges. Extend focused coverage for the new query boundary, fresh active-club authority and transient-state preservation without claiming later interest-mapping proof.

Existing feature-level LiveView tests exercise admission/removal command behavior, projector-driven open-view updates and reconnect-sensitive command state. They must continue passing after dashboard fields move under one result assign.
Targeted-add coverage protects routed target resolution, confirmation, success/focus state and authorization behavior that must remain LiveView-owned across dashboard result replacement.

LiveView state changes should use assigns consistently; focused LiveView tests should assert rendered outcomes with selectors, and transient forms must remain `to_form/2`-backed rather than being replaced by query refreshes.
Keep modules in separate files, use focused Mix test files, and avoid sleeps in process tests; deterministic synchronization should be used where process ordering must be proved.
Any HEEx edits must retain component form usage, unique DOM IDs and valid HEEx interpolation and conditional syntax.

constraints: Preserve every existing dashboard URL, rendered DOM contract and user-visible behavior; this task introduces a read boundary, not a visual redesign.

The authenticated normalized email is the durable query input. A stale `current_identity_clubs` snapshot may remain only if another unchanged shell concern requires it, but it must not authorize the dashboard query or refresh.

The coherent dashboard result is the source of truth for projection-backed display and authorization fields. Do not retain compatibility mirrors for selected club/group, members, counts, messages or permissions in socket state.
A render-local expansion of the dashboard map is allowed to keep the template change bounded because it does not create independently refreshed socket state.
Subscribe only for a connected LiveView and do so before the connected query invocation. Do not claim this ordering alone closes the bind-time race; task 004 owns deterministic reconciliation.

Preserve the existing manual notification predicates exactly enough to avoid expanding task scope. Their known over-broad and missing cases are intentional pending work, not behavior to bless as the target design.
Preserve existing `:forbidden` and `:not_found` transitions and never retain the previous private dashboard result when the fresh query returns an access error.
Keep active section, route IDs, targeted-member focus/success, picker form/query/open state, removal operation state, access-request state, flash and navigation outside the dashboard result.
Do not nest a new query or view-model module inside another module.
Use focused, deterministic tests and do not use `Process.sleep/1`.
completion_evidence_required: List every changed path and identify the app query entry point and the single dashboard socket assign.
Show focused test evidence that the query refetches active clubs from authenticated email on every call and rejects a selected club after membership loss despite a stale mount-time snapshot.
Show focused LiveView evidence that route/access semantics and successful refresh behavior remain correct after projection-backed fields move under the coherent dashboard result.
Show evidence that at least one meaningful transient dashboard state survives a successful query-result replacement, with the remaining existing admission, removal and targeted-add suites passing.

Confirm by source inspection that connected subscription occurs before the query call, refreshes no longer authorize through `current_identity_clubs`, and existing notification predicates were not broadened or presented as the final adapter.
Report the exact focused validation commands, exit statuses and concise pass summaries, plus any unresolved issue without marking the task complete.

current_worker_packet.outcome: The club dashboard loads and refreshes one coherent dashboard view model from the authenticated email and freshly resolved active-club authority, stores that result under one socket assign, subscribes before the connected initial read, and preserves existing route, access, rendering, command and transient-state behavior while the current notification predicates remain provisional.
scope: Add an app-owned `MembaWeb.MemberDashboardQuery` boundary, with focused tests, that accepts the routed club identity, authenticated normalized email and selected group identity; every invocation must call `Accounts.list_active_clubs_for_email/1`, construct only the identity input needed by `MemberDashboardPresentation`, and return its coherent result or the existing `:forbidden`/`:not_found` error.

Change `MemberDashboardLive.mount/3`, `handle_params/3`, explicit command refreshes and notification refreshes to use the new query. On connected mount, subscribe to `Memba.ReadModelChanges.topic/0` before invoking the query; disconnected mount must still perform the current read.

Keep the routed club ID and authenticated identity email as stable LiveView inputs. Do not derive a later query input from the previously loaded `selected_club`, and do not use mount-captured `current_identity_clubs` as authorization for a refresh.

Store the projection-backed dashboard result under one long-lived socket assign such as `:dashboard`. Adapt event handlers and helper functions to read selected club, selected group, current member, permission flags, rows and counts from that model instead of retaining mirrored top-level socket assigns.

Adapt rendering to consume the coherent model without duplicating all of its fields into socket state. A render-local map expansion for the existing template is acceptable; if Phoenix shell metadata requires a derived `:page_title`, keep the dashboard result as its sole source and do not perform an independent read.

Preserve current `:forbidden` versus `:not_found` behavior on mount, route patches and refreshes, and preserve existing command behavior for access requests, admissions, removals and welcome delivery.

Retain the current hand-written `handle_info/2` matching semantics provisionally, including their current broad and missing cases. This slice changes their refresh target to the new query but does not introduce interests, a source adapter, bind-window reconciliation or new projector coverage.

Add focused proof that repeated query calls use fresh active-club authority, that selected-club membership loss cannot be masked by a mount-time club snapshot, that route changes still re-evaluate selected-group access, and that successful refreshes do not reset picker/query, targeted-add, removal, access-request or command feedback state. Preserve existing dashboard, admission and targeted-add regression coverage.

references.facts: The technical model requires one coherent dashboard query result, fresh authorization on every refresh, LiveView-owned subscription, subscribe-before-read ordering and preservation of transient state. The broader bind-time reconciliation, scoped invalidation and conversation proof remain later obligations.

ADR 0027 requires each view-specific query to return one coherent view model for one assign, with an authorized reread on relevant changes; club home must begin as one dashboard model rather than separately refreshed fields.

Committed projection notifications are broadcast on the shared PubSub topic as `{:read_model_changed, %{projector: ..., source_event: ..., metadata: ..., changes: ...}}`. This task retains the dashboard's current filters but moves subscription before the connected read.

The accepted matrix records that MemberDashboardLive currently spreads one composed result across ordinary assigns, reads before subscribing and refreshes with mount-captured active clubs. It identifies route IDs, picker/admission/removal/access-request state as LiveView-owned and requires fresh authority beginning from authenticated email.

`mount/3` currently calls `MemberDashboardPresentation.load/4` before subscribing and fans `dashboard_assigns` into the socket. `refresh_dashboard/3` reuses `current_identity_clubs`; handlers and command helpers read selected club, selected group, current member and permission flags from top-level assigns. Existing handle_info clauses broadly refresh for all MemberEmailDelivery changes and same-club configured projectors.

`load/4` already composes selected club/member authorization, discoverable and participating groups, permissions, members, counts, conversations, admission candidates and group email data into one result map. It accepts caller-supplied active clubs, so the new query must supply a fresh list on every invocation while preserving `:forbidden` and `:not_found` distinctions.

`Accounts.list_active_clubs_for_email/1` normalizes the email and reads the current active club projections. It is the required fresh starting point instead of `current_identity_clubs` captured during mount.

The dashboard template currently consumes flat assigns for selected club/group, groups, permissions, member rows, counts and message rows. Rendering may expand the coherent dashboard model locally, but these values must no longer be duplicated as long-lived socket assigns.

Existing coverage includes routed rendering, group discovery, access loss, route-patch authorization rechecks, current-actor role loss, conversation-access changes, member rows/counts and initial role badges. Extend focused coverage for the new query boundary, fresh active-club authority and transient-state preservation without claiming later interest-mapping proof.

Existing feature-level LiveView tests exercise admission/removal command behavior, projector-driven open-view updates and reconnect-sensitive command state. They must continue passing after dashboard fields move under one result assign.
Targeted-add coverage protects routed target resolution, confirmation, success/focus state and authorization behavior that must remain LiveView-owned across dashboard result replacement.

LiveView state changes should use assigns consistently; focused LiveView tests should assert rendered outcomes with selectors, and transient forms must remain `to_form/2`-backed rather than being replaced by query refreshes.
Keep modules in separate files, use focused Mix test files, and avoid sleeps in process tests; deterministic synchronization should be used where process ordering must be proved.
Any HEEx edits must retain component form usage, unique DOM IDs and valid HEEx interpolation and conditional syntax.

constraints: Preserve every existing dashboard URL, rendered DOM contract and user-visible behavior; this task introduces a read boundary, not a visual redesign.

The authenticated normalized email is the durable query input. A stale `current_identity_clubs` snapshot may remain only if another unchanged shell concern requires it, but it must not authorize the dashboard query or refresh.

The coherent dashboard result is the source of truth for projection-backed display and authorization fields. Do not retain compatibility mirrors for selected club/group, members, counts, messages or permissions in socket state.
A render-local expansion of the dashboard map is allowed to keep the template change bounded because it does not create independently refreshed socket state.
Subscribe only for a connected LiveView and do so before the connected query invocation. Do not claim this ordering alone closes the bind-time race; task 004 owns deterministic reconciliation.

Preserve the existing manual notification predicates exactly enough to avoid expanding task scope. Their known over-broad and missing cases are intentional pending work, not behavior to bless as the target design.
Preserve existing `:forbidden` and `:not_found` transitions and never retain the previous private dashboard result when the fresh query returns an access error.
Keep active section, route IDs, targeted-member focus/success, picker form/query/open state, removal operation state, access-request state, flash and navigation outside the dashboard result.
Do not nest a new query or view-model module inside another module.
Use focused, deterministic tests and do not use `Process.sleep/1`.
completion_evidence_required: List every changed path and identify the app query entry point and the single dashboard socket assign.
Show focused test evidence that the query refetches active clubs from authenticated email on every call and rejects a selected club after membership loss despite a stale mount-time snapshot.
Show focused LiveView evidence that route/access semantics and successful refresh behavior remain correct after projection-backed fields move under the coherent dashboard result.
Show evidence that at least one meaningful transient dashboard state survives a successful query-result replacement, with the remaining existing admission, removal and targeted-add suites passing.

Confirm by source inspection that connected subscription occurs before the query call, refreshes no longer authorize through `current_identity_clubs`, and existing notification predicates were not broadened or presented as the final adapter.
Report the exact focused validation commands, exit statuses and concise pass summaries, plus any unresolved issue without marking the task complete.

resume_gate.notes:
Script completed: set -eu
PLAN_PATH='docs/iterations/067-live-projection-queries/plan.md'
case "$PLAN_PATH" in
  */plan.md) ITERATION_DIR=${PLAN_PATH%/plan.md} ;;
  *) echo "plan_path must end with /plan.md: $PLAN_PATH" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
TODO_PATH="$ITERATION_DIR/todo.md"
echo '=== Iteration resume gate ==='
if git rev-parse --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf 'HEAD: ' && git log -1 --format='%h %s'
else
  echo 'HEAD: unavailable'
fi
if [ -f "$TODO_PATH" ]; then
  checked=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*- \[x\] ' "$TODO_PATH" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  unchecked=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*- \[ \] ' "$TODO_PATH" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  printf 'Todo: %s (%s checked, %s unchecked)\n' "$TODO_PATH" "${checked:-0}" "${unchecked:-0}"
else
  printf 'Todo: %s is absent; sync_task_list will create it from plan.md.\n' "$TODO_PATH"
fi
status=$(git status --short)
if [ -n "$status" ]; then
  echo 'Uncommitted changes present:'
  printf '%s\n' "$status"
  echo 'Refusing to resume with a dirty working tree. Commit, stash, or run git reset --hard HEAD (and clean untracked files if appropriate), then rerun iteration-implementation.' >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo 'Working tree clean; safe to resume from durable Fabro checkpoint commits.'

if git rev-parse --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf 'HEAD: ' && git log -1 --format='%h %s'
else
  echo 'HEAD: unavailable'

  checked=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*- \[x\] ' "$TODO_PATH" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')

else
  printf 'Todo: %s is absent; sync_task_list will create it from plan.md.\n' "$TODO_PATH"
fi
status=$(git status --short)
if [ -n "$status" ]; then
  echo 'Uncommitted changes present:'
  printf '%s\n' "$status"
  echo 'Refusing to resume with a dirty working tree. Commit, stash, or run git reset --hard HEAD (and clean untracked files if appropriate), then rerun iteration-implementation.' >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo 'Working tree clean; safe to resume from durable Fabro checkpoint commits.'

The candidate changed the dashboard query, LiveView and focused tests and reported 85 focused tests passing. Those changes remain unaccepted candidate work and must be preserved while addressing the review gap.

Successful mount currently assigns only `:dashboard`, successful `refresh_dashboard/2` replacements also assign only `:dashboard`, and `render/1` expands the dashboard map only into render-local assigns. That expansion is too late to supply LiveView shell metadata.

The root layout's `<.live_title>` reads `assigns[:page_title]`, defaults to `Memba`, and appends ` · Memba`; therefore the LiveView socket must carry the derived top-level title for initial rendering and title diffs.
The coherent dashboard result already contains `page_title: selected_club.name`; this value is the sole permitted source for shell title metadata and no extra club read is needed.

The focused LiveView suite already builds a signed-in routed club dashboard and is the appropriate place to assert `page_title(view) == "Alpine Club · Memba"` while retaining existing route, access and transient-state coverage.

The plan requires one coherent dashboard query result bound to one assign while preserving existing page behavior. Deriving shell metadata from that result does not split the query or authorize an independent read.
ADR 0027 requires club home to begin with one coherent dashboard view model rather than separately refreshed projection fields; the revision must keep `:dashboard` as that one result.
LiveView state changes should be made through socket assigns and focused LiveView tests should assert rendered behavior using the framework's test APIs.

current_worker_packet.todo_line: - [ ] 003 Introduce and focused-test an app-owned dashboard query/view-model boundary that begins from the authenticated email and fresh active-club authority; move all projection-backed dashboard data behind one coherent socket assign, subscribe before the connected initial read, preserve route/access error semantics and transient LiveView state, and retain the existing notification predicates provisionally.
current_worker_packet.outcome: Restore the club-specific browser title while preserving `:dashboard` as the sole projection-query result assign by deriving the LiveView shell's top-level `:page_title` metadata from each successfully installed dashboard result, with focused regression coverage.
scope: Update the successful initial dashboard installation and every successful dashboard refresh so the socket receives both the coherent `:dashboard` query result and a top-level `:page_title` derived only from `dashboard.page_title`.
Prefer one small installation helper or equivalent shared path so initial mount and refresh cannot diverge; the helper must not perform another read or mirror any other dashboard fields.

Add a focused `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion proving that the routed club dashboard retains its club-specific title, including the root layout suffix, after the single-result-assign migration.

Retain all accepted parts of the existing task-003 candidate: fresh email-based authority, one dashboard result assign, connected subscribe-before-read ordering, current route/access transitions, provisional notification predicates and transient-state preservation.
scope_exclusions: Do not move additional dashboard fields back to top-level socket assigns; `:page_title` is permitted shell metadata, not a second query result.
Do not redesign the root layout or change title text, suffix behavior, dashboard rendering, URLs, DOM structure or user-facing copy.
Do not implement opaque interests, scoped notification translation, bind-time reconciliation, reconnect machinery or subscriber cleanup from tasks 004 and 005.
Do not broaden or otherwise revise the provisional projector predicates.

Do not change conversation detail, another LiveView, the local package, Mix/Docker/quality-gate integration, acceptance features, ADRs, the approved plan, migration matrix, todo file or delivery artifacts.

references.facts: The latest review accepted the candidate's fresh authority, coherent `:dashboard` result, subscribe-before-read ordering, provisional predicates and transient-state proof, but requires revision because the root layout reads `socket.assigns.page_title`; it specifically requests deriving that shell assign from `dashboard.page_title` and adding a `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion.

The candidate changed the dashboard query, LiveView and focused tests and reported 85 focused tests passing. Those changes remain unaccepted candidate work and must be preserved while addressing the review gap.

Successful mount currently assigns only `:dashboard`, successful `refresh_dashboard/2` replacements also assign only `:dashboard`, and `render/1` expands the dashboard map only into render-local assigns. That expansion is too late to supply LiveView shell metadata.

The root layout's `<.live_title>` reads `assigns[:page_title]`, defaults to `Memba`, and appends ` · Memba`; therefore the LiveView socket must carry the derived top-level title for initial rendering and title diffs.
The coherent dashboard result already contains `page_title: selected_club.name`; this value is the sole permitted source for shell title metadata and no extra club read is needed.

The focused LiveView suite already builds a signed-in routed club dashboard and is the appropriate place to assert `page_title(view) == "Alpine Club · Memba"` while retaining existing route, access and transient-state coverage.

The plan requires one coherent dashboard query result bound to one assign while preserving existing page behavior. Deriving shell metadata from that result does not split the query or authorize an independent read.
ADR 0027 requires club home to begin with one coherent dashboard view model rather than separately refreshed projection fields; the revision must keep `:dashboard` as that one result.
LiveView state changes should be made through socket assigns and focused LiveView tests should assert rendered behavior using the framework's test APIs.

constraints: Keep the task identity `task-003` and preserve the candidate provenance; this is a bounded revision, not a new implementation task.
The top-level `:page_title` must always be derived from the dashboard result being installed and must not come from a separate query, stale selected-club assign or mount-time club snapshot.
Apply the derivation on both initial success and refresh success so future title-changing dashboard results cannot leave shell metadata stale.
Keep `:dashboard` as the sole projection-backed query-result assign; do not restore selected club, selected group, rows, counts, messages or permissions as top-level compatibility mirrors.
Preserve existing `:forbidden` and `:not_found` behavior and all current transient LiveView state.
Use focused deterministic tests and do not use `Process.sleep/1`.
Do not mark the todo line complete; return evidence for review.
completion_evidence_required: List every changed path and identify the shared initial/refresh dashboard-installation path, if introduced.
Show the exact `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion and its expected club-specific title including the ` · Memba` suffix.

Confirm by source inspection that top-level `:page_title` is derived only from the newly installed dashboard result on both mount and refresh, with no independent read or additional mirrored projection fields.
Report exact focused validation commands, exit statuses and concise pass summaries.
Report any unresolved issue without marking task 003 complete.

PLAN_PATH='docs/iterations/067-live-projection-queries/plan.md'

esac
TODO_PATH="$ITERATION_DIR/todo.md"
echo '=== Iteration resume gate ==='
if git rev-parse --verify HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf 'HEAD: ' && git log -1 --format='%h %s'
else
  echo 'HEAD: unavailable'
fi
if [ -f "$TODO_PATH" ]; then
  checked=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*- \[x\] ' "$TODO_PATH" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  unchecked=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*- \[ \] ' "$TODO_PATH" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  printf 'Todo: %s (%s checked, %s unchecked)\n' "$TODO_PATH" "${checked:-0}" "${unchecked:-0}"
else
  printf 'Todo: %s is absent; sync_task_list will create it from plan.md.\n' "$TODO_PATH"
fi
status=$(git status --short)
if [ -n "$status" ]; then
  echo 'Uncommitted changes present:'
  printf '%s\n' "$status"
  echo 'Refusing to resume with a dirty working tree. Commit, stash, or run git reset --hard HEAD (and clean untracked files if appropriate), then rerun iteration-implementation.' >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo 'Working tree clean; safe to resume from durable Fabro checkpoint commits.'

The candidate changed the dashboard query, LiveView and focused tests and reported 85 focused tests passing. Those changes remain unaccepted candidate work and must be preserved while addressing the review gap.

Successful mount currently assigns only `:dashboard`, successful `refresh_dashboard/2` replacements also assign only `:dashboard`, and `render/1` expands the dashboard map only into render-local assigns. That expansion is too late to supply LiveView shell metadata.

The root layout's `<.live_title>` reads `assigns[:page_title]`, defaults to `Memba`, and appends ` · Memba`; therefore the LiveView socket must carry the derived top-level title for initial rendering and title diffs.
The coherent dashboard result already contains `page_title: selected_club.name`; this value is the sole permitted source for shell title metadata and no extra club read is needed.

The focused LiveView suite already builds a signed-in routed club dashboard and is the appropriate place to assert `page_title(view) == "Alpine Club · Memba"` while retaining existing route, access and transient-state coverage.

The plan requires one coherent dashboard query result bound to one assign while preserving existing page behavior. Deriving shell metadata from that result does not split the query or authorize an independent read.
ADR 0027 requires club home to begin with one coherent dashboard view model rather than separately refreshed projection fields; the revision must keep `:dashboard` as that one result.
LiveView state changes should be made through socket assigns and focused LiveView tests should assert rendered behavior using the framework's test APIs.

current_worker_packet.outcome: Restore the club-specific browser title while preserving `:dashboard` as the sole projection-query result assign by deriving the LiveView shell's top-level `:page_title` metadata from each successfully installed dashboard result, with focused regression coverage.
scope: Update the successful initial dashboard installation and every successful dashboard refresh so the socket receives both the coherent `:dashboard` query result and a top-level `:page_title` derived only from `dashboard.page_title`.
Prefer one small installation helper or equivalent shared path so initial mount and refresh cannot diverge; the helper must not perform another read or mirror any other dashboard fields.

Add a focused `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion proving that the routed club dashboard retains its club-specific title, including the root layout suffix, after the single-result-assign migration.

Retain all accepted parts of the existing task-003 candidate: fresh email-based authority, one dashboard result assign, connected subscribe-before-read ordering, current route/access transitions, provisional notification predicates and transient-state preservation.
scope_exclusions: Do not move additional dashboard fields back to top-level socket assigns; `:page_title` is permitted shell metadata, not a second query result.
Do not redesign the root layout or change title text, suffix behavior, dashboard rendering, URLs, DOM structure or user-facing copy.
Do not implement opaque interests, scoped notification translation, bind-time reconciliation, reconnect machinery or subscriber cleanup from tasks 004 and 005.
Do not broaden or otherwise revise the provisional projector predicates.

Do not change conversation detail, another LiveView, the local package, Mix/Docker/quality-gate integration, acceptance features, ADRs, the approved plan, migration matrix, todo file or delivery artifacts.

references.facts: The latest review accepted the candidate's fresh authority, coherent `:dashboard` result, subscribe-before-read ordering, provisional predicates and transient-state proof, but requires revision because the root layout reads `socket.assigns.page_title`; it specifically requests deriving that shell assign from `dashboard.page_title` and adding a `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion.

The candidate changed the dashboard query, LiveView and focused tests and reported 85 focused tests passing. Those changes remain unaccepted candidate work and must be preserved while addressing the review gap.

Successful mount currently assigns only `:dashboard`, successful `refresh_dashboard/2` replacements also assign only `:dashboard`, and `render/1` expands the dashboard map only into render-local assigns. That expansion is too late to supply LiveView shell metadata.

The root layout's `<.live_title>` reads `assigns[:page_title]`, defaults to `Memba`, and appends ` · Memba`; therefore the LiveView socket must carry the derived top-level title for initial rendering and title diffs.
The coherent dashboard result already contains `page_title: selected_club.name`; this value is the sole permitted source for shell title metadata and no extra club read is needed.

The focused LiveView suite already builds a signed-in routed club dashboard and is the appropriate place to assert `page_title(view) == "Alpine Club · Memba"` while retaining existing route, access and transient-state coverage.

The plan requires one coherent dashboard query result bound to one assign while preserving existing page behavior. Deriving shell metadata from that result does not split the query or authorize an independent read.
ADR 0027 requires club home to begin with one coherent dashboard view model rather than separately refreshed projection fields; the revision must keep `:dashboard` as that one result.
LiveView state changes should be made through socket assigns and focused LiveView tests should assert rendered behavior using the framework's test APIs.

constraints: Keep the task identity `task-003` and preserve the candidate provenance; this is a bounded revision, not a new implementation task.
The top-level `:page_title` must always be derived from the dashboard result being installed and must not come from a separate query, stale selected-club assign or mount-time club snapshot.
Apply the derivation on both initial success and refresh success so future title-changing dashboard results cannot leave shell metadata stale.
Keep `:dashboard` as the sole projection-backed query-result assign; do not restore selected club, selected group, rows, counts, messages or permissions as top-level compatibility mirrors.
Preserve existing `:forbidden` and `:not_found` behavior and all current transient LiveView state.
Use focused deterministic tests and do not use `Process.sleep/1`.
Do not mark the todo line complete; return evidence for review.
completion_evidence_required: List every changed path and identify the shared initial/refresh dashboard-installation path, if introduced.
Show the exact `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.page_title/1` assertion and its expected club-specific title including the ` · Memba` suffix.

Confirm by source inspection that top-level `:page_title` is derived only from the newly installed dashboard result on both mount and refresh, with no independent read or additional mirrored projection fields.
Report exact focused validation commands, exit statuses and concise pass summaries.
Report any unresolved issue without marking task 003 complete.

Retain all accepted parts of the existing task-003 candidate: fresh email-based authority, one dashboard result assign, connected subscribe-before-read ordering, current route/access transitions, provisional notification predicates and transient-state preservation.
scope_exclusions: Do not move additional dashboard fields back to top-level socket assigns; `:page_title` is permitted shell metadata, not a second query result.
Do not redesign the root layout or change title text, suffix behavior, dashboard rendering, URLs, DOM structure or user-facing copy.
Do not implement opaque interests, scoped notification translation, bind-time reconciliation, reconnect machinery or subscriber cleanup from tasks 004 and 005.
Do not broaden or otherwise revise the provisional projector predicates.

The candidate changed the dashboard query, LiveView and focused tests and reported 85 focused tests passing. Those changes remain unaccepted candidate work and must be preserved while addressing the review gap.

Successful mount currently assigns only `:dashboard`, successful `refresh_dashboard/2` replacements also assign only `:dashboard`, and `render/1` expands the dashboard map only into render-local assigns. That expansion is too late to supply LiveView shell metadata.

ADR 0027 requires club home to begin with one coherent dashboard view model rather than separately refreshed projection fields; the revision must keep `:dashboard` as that one result.
LiveView state changes should be made through socket assigns and focused LiveView tests should assert rendered behavior using the framework's test APIs.

constraints: Keep the task identity `task-003` and preserve the candidate provenance; this is a bounded revision, not a new implementation task.
The top-level `:page_title` must always be derived from the dashboard result being installed and must not come from a separate query, stale selected-club assign or mount-time club snapshot.
Apply the derivation on both initial success and refresh success so future title-changing dashboard results cannot leave shell metadata stale.
Keep `:dashboard` as the sole projection-backed query-result assign; do not restore selected club, selected group, rows, counts, messages or permissions as top-level compatibility mirrors.
Preserve existing `:forbidden` and `:not_found` behavior and all current transient LiveView state.
Use focused deterministic tests and do not use `Process.sleep/1`.
Do not mark the todo line complete; return evidence for review.
completion_evidence_required: List every changed path and identify the shared initial/refresh dashboard-installation path, if introduced.

Confirm by source inspection that top-level `:page_title` is derived only from the newly installed dashboard result on both mount and refresh, with no independent read or additional mirrored projection fields.
Report exact focused validation commands, exit statuses and concise pass summaries.
Report any unresolved issue without marking task 003 complete.

agent_tools.name: apply_patch
agent_tools.description: Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

agent_tools.name: close_agent
agent_tools.description: Close a running or completed subagent that is no longer needed.

agent_tools.name: request_user_input
agent_tools.description: Ask the human one or more questions and wait for their answers before continuing this stage.

agent_tools.name: send_input
agent_tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running agent receives it at a safe turn boundary. A completed agent starts another turn in the same session with its existing history.

agent_tools.name: shell_command
agent_tools.description:
Runs a shell command and returns its output.
- Always set the `workdir` param rather than using `cd`.
- Reading and searching files goes through this tool: prefer `rg` and `rg --files`, which are much faster than alternatives like `grep` and `find`.
- Use `apply_patch` to edit files, not `cat`, heredocs, or other shell write tricks.
- `timeout_ms` defaults to 10000 ms and is capped at 600000 ms. A command that timed out once will time out again, so raise the timeout rather than retrying.

agent_tools.name: spawn_agent
agent_tools.description: Spawn a subagent for independent work or context isolation. Use it for tasks that can proceed separately, and avoid duplicating the same work in the parent session.

agent_tools.name: update_plan
agent_tools.description: Update the multi-step plan for the current task. Submit the entire plan; existing steps are reconciled by exact step text.

agent_tools.name: wait
agent_tools.description: Wait for a subagent to complete, then use the result to synthesize the outcome for the user.
